newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil driven higher by IPEs and demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil driven higher by IPEs and demand.

text.p: NWE gas oil ended stronger on Wednesday as futures soared and demand in the physical market buoyed premiums, traders said.
The September contract closed $3.75 higher at $221.75 a tonne reducing the Sept/Oct spread to $5.25.

On the heating oil barge market, a few parcels for traded at Sept +25 to +50 cents, fob ARA for delivery next week. Traders said the prompt situation was still very tight but that most players appeared to be keeping out of the market ahead of the September contract's expiry on Thursday.

On the cargo market, the U.S./Europe arbitrage door was still ajar, but traders said the number of cargoes heading for Europe would be limited by the fact few U.S. refiners make the correct specifications for Europe.
On the low sulphur front, premiums were put at Oct IPE +$16/+$17, cif Le Havre.
Traders said 0.2 percent quality material continued to be tight as the heating oil market picked up across NWE, boosting premiums on Russian as well as NWE cargoes.
There was talk a German heating oil cargo traded at Oct IPE +$7.75, cif Hamburg. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714
